messages.subject: Re:  NBLAST: Tangent calculation method
parts:
﻿
Dear Robert,

Thanks for your message and interest in NBLAST. There are two methods for calculating the tangent vectors. One is used when the input is any collection of points (including neurons). See  http://natverse.org/nat/reference/dotprops.html 

This is actually what we use and recommend  and matches the description below. Furthermore it is the only method which has been statistically calibrated for Drosophila neurons, for which we recommend the following settings 

myneurons.dps=dotprops(myneurons, resample=1, k=5)

The second method makes some use of knowledge of the parent of a point. This is used if you supply nblast with a neuron without first calculating the dotprops representation. This appears to be what you are using, but I’m afraid it’s not the recommended approach as it has not been properly explored. Furthermore if you are repeatedly nblasting many neurons (eg calculating all by all nblast matrices) it will be quite a lot slower as the tangent vector calculation takes some time and will be repeated for every comparison (eg 800 calculations for 20 neurons instead of 20 if you precompute). 

You are of course welcome to reimplement NBLAST eg in another language. In fact there is already some work in progress eg here:

https://github.com/clbarnes/nblast-rs

(Rust with Python bindings). And here

https://github.com/seung-lab/RealNeuralNetworks.jl/

(In Julia)

If you are hoping to make it faster you will find that it is hard but not impossible — the R version is already fast because it spends most of the compute time in a C++ nearest neighbour library. See eg discussion here:

https://github.com/clbarnes/nblast-rs/issues/20

All the best,

Greg. 


Sent from my iPhone

On 6 May 2020, at 22:22, Robert Alfredson <robert.c....@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Dear Dr. Jefferis,

I hope you are well! My name is Robert Alfredson, and I am a research assistant in the lab of Dr. Rebecca Yang at Duke University. We make frequent use of your tools, especially for image registration and processing neuron skeletons.

One recent project of ours implements NBLAST search, and I would like please to ask a question about the score calculation. In the NBLAST paper, there is a method described of calculating the tangent via the eigenvector of an SVD based on the five nearest neighbors to the node in question. However, in the NBLAST code, the tangent appears to be calculated as the vector that points to the node in question from its parent.

I have observed that the latter method yields accurate results, and want to ask about why it came to replace the SVD method, e.g., perhaps it enhanced performance without impacting accuracy? Thanks very much!

Sincerely,

Robert
